literal: Virtue ocean gracious-one feet those-who-reached except, other oceans crossing difficult.
translation: Except for those who hold onto the feet of the gracious one who is an ocean of virtue, it is difficult to cross other oceans.
modern: அறக்கடலாக விளங்கும் அந்தணனின் திருவடிகளை அடைந்தவர்களுக்கே அன்றி, மற்றவர்களால் பிறவிக் கடல்களைக் கடப்பது கடினம்.
explanation: This couplet compares the divine to an ocean of virtue (அறவாழி) and worldly existence to other oceans (பிறவாழி). The term 'அந்தணன்' is used here to denote a being of ultimate grace and righteousness. The poet explains that only by seeking refuge in the feet of this gracious guide can one hope to cross the difficult oceans of worldly attachments and rebirths. Without this spiritual anchor, navigating the trials of life remains an impossible task.
